title: The Lighter Brief
overview: Today's brief is mostly practical news. Gas finally dipped below $4 a gallon, Charlotte has new street-vending rules, and there's a useful update for anyone on Ozempic-style medications. There's also a promising sleep apnea result, a fresh reggae release, and the start of one last season of Love & Hip Hop.

stories.headline: NC attorney general sues a Gastonia driving school
stories.summary: North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson is suing NC Virtual Driver's Ed and its owner. His office accuses them of charging families for behind-the-wheel lessons that weren't given and refusing refunds and completion certificates. One parent said her daughter got only two hours of road time and had to pay $350 to finish driver's ed elsewhere.
key_facts: More than 50 people complained to the AG's office and the DMV.
The DMV revoked the school's license in September.
The owner is named as Courtney Elizabeth Brazil.
The school didn't respond to reporters in time for the reports.
disputed: These are allegations in a lawsuit. No court has ruled yet.
stories.why: The goal is to get money back for affected families, and it's a good reminder to check a driving school's license before paying up front.

stories.headline: Charlotte expands street vending limits citywide
stories.summary: Charlotte City Council voted 8-1 on Monday to restrict merchandise sales on streets and sidewalks across the whole city, not just uptown and the stadium areas. The ordinance also sets up a system for permitted 'peddlers' marketplaces' and lets licensed vendors apply to sell at sanctioned festivals and events.
key_facts: The vote was 8-1, on Monday.
Newspapers and magazines are excluded from the ban.
Vendors need a permit and a spot pre-approved by Center City Partners.
The application fee and the locations of new marketplaces haven't been set.
disputed: Reports differ on penalties. WBTV describes a possible misdemeanor for a third non-food violation within 30 days, while WCNC's headline says there are no criminal penalties.
It's unclear how the rules apply to food vendors and food trucks.
stories.why: If you sell at, or shop from, sidewalk vendors in Charlotte, where and how they can set up is changing.

stories.headline: Diesel cleanup underway near Atrium Health Mercy
stories.summary: Diesel fuel leaked from a storage tank at Atrium Health's Mercy Hospital in Charlotte over the weekend, and some of it reached a Briar Creek tributary through storm drains. Cleanup is in progress and the EPA is monitoring it.
key_facts: Storm Water Services estimates about 2,000 gallons leaked from the tank.
One report puts the amount at up to 800 gallons.
The EPA is monitoring the cleanup.
disputed: The two figures appear in different reports. The shorter reports don't make clear whether 800 gallons refers to the total leak or the portion that reached the creek.
stories.why: Crews are on it, and it's handy to know if you spend time along Briar Creek.

links.title: Cleanup underway after Atrium Health hospital diesel fuel leak into Briar Creek

stories.headline: Jamaica says it spent nothing on the scrapped Cardi B concert
stories.summary: Jamaica's culture ministry says the government made no payments or commitments toward a proposed concert featuring Cardi B, calling it a private commercial event. The statement comes amid a dispute between Cardi B and the organizers of BZR WKND after she withdrew from the show.
key_facts: The show was originally scheduled for October 16–18.
The government says it is limiting event spending to focus on recovery after Hurricane Melissa.
disputed: Confirmed: the ministry's statement that it paid no fees.
Reported: Cardi B has threatened legal action against the organizers, and the details of that dispute aren't laid out here.
stories.why: It clears up where public money did and didn't go while Jamaica focuses on rebuilding.

links.title: No gov’t funds committed to proposed Cardi B concert, says Ministry

stories.headline: Jamaican dollar holds steady
stories.summary: The US dollar ended Tuesday at J$159.07, barely changed from the day before, according to the Bank of Jamaica. The Canadian dollar and British pound both slipped against the Jamaican dollar.
key_facts: US dollar: J$159.07, down from J$159.09.
Canadian dollar: J$112.17, down from J$113.61.
British pound: J$211.87, down from J$214.53.
stories.why: It's a quick check-in if you send money to or from Jamaica.

stories.headline: New Vortex Riddim drops November 13
stories.summary: French producer David Attal's four-track Vortex Riddim arrives November 13 through VPAL Music, with four artists each putting their own spin on the same rhythm. Nigy Boy's love-and-unity track 'Where Is The Love' and Vanzo's 'Spotlight' are already out.
key_facts: The release date is November 13 via VPAL Music.
The artists are Nigy Boy, Vanzo, Darrio and Denham Smith.
It's produced under Attal's Stargate Productions label.
stories.why: It's fresh reggae for your weekend, and Attal describes it as 'four artistes, four identities, but one VORTEX universe.'

links.title: Nigy Boy, Vanzo lead Stargate’s Vortex Riddim ahead of November 13 release

stories.headline: FDA adds a rare eye-risk warning to GLP-1 drugs
stories.summary: The FDA is requiring 12 GLP-1 drugs, including Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, Zepbound and Foundayo, to list a rare eye condition called NAION in their label warnings. NAION involves reduced blood flow to the optic nerve and can cause sudden vision loss. The FDA reviewed trial, real-world and observational data and found a higher relative risk, though the absolute risk stays very low.
key_facts: The FDA announced it on Monday, Nov. 9.
In pooled trials, NAION occurred at 6.4 per 100,000 patient-years on GLP-1s, compared with 3.8 on placebo or other treatments.
The review was prompted by a 2025 JAMA Ophthalmology study of 175,000 people with diabetes.
disputed: These are already FDA-approved drugs. This is a label safety update, not a recall.
Animal data showed no clear way the drugs would cause NAION, and its risk factors overlap with conditions common in GLP-1 patients.
Lilly says the notice isn't specific to its medicines.
stories.why: If you take one of these drugs, it's worth knowing the signs of sudden vision changes and talking to your doctor instead of stopping on your own.

links.title: FDA orders new eye risk be listed on a dozen GLP-1s, including Novo's Ozempic, Lilly's Zepbound

stories.headline: Lilly's GLP-1 pill eased sleep apnea in a big trial
stories.summary: In a year-long phase 3 trial, Lilly's oral GLP-1 Foundayo (orforglipron) cut sleep apnea breathing interruptions in adults with excess weight, compared with placebo. Participants also lost about 11% of their body weight. Lilly plans to approach the FDA about adding sleep apnea to the label.
key_facts: The trial had 712 patients across two studies, with and without PAP machines.
Without PAP, episodes dropped 43.8% (21.1 per hour), compared with 4.3 per hour on placebo.
About 31.5% of the non-PAP group reached remission or mild disease.
Results were presented at the American Heart Association meeting and published in JAMA.
disputed: These are late-stage (phase 3) results, described as preliminary.
Foundayo isn't approved for sleep apnea yet, and an FDA application is still to come.
The new FDA eye-risk warning on GLP-1s also covers Foundayo.
stories.why: Many people struggle with CPAP masks, so a daily pill option could be a big quality-of-life win if it's approved.

links.title: Lilly looks to gird Foundayo label after late-stage win in sleep apnea
